intro.title: Lift Right
lines: Five loads, one back. First size up each load and choose how to move it.
Then do the lift yourself. Keys: A / D to step, S to bend your knees, W to straighten up, SPACE to grip and to let go. Mouse: hold the arrow pad under the gauge, and click GRIP.
Your back hinges over whatever your knees and your distance leave it — watch the SPINE LOAD gauge and keep it under the line.
Time spent over that line drains your Back Health. Protect it — it has to last a whole career.

lifts.name: Small parts box
lifts.prompt: A 12 lb box on the floor needs to go on the pallet behind you.

options.text: Lift it myself — with good form
options.feedback: Light, compact load: a solo lift with good form is the right call.
Safe, but overkill for 12 lb. Save team lifts for heavy or awkward loads.

lifts.name: Case of copy paper
lifts.prompt: A 40 lb case of paper. Compact, with good hand-holds.

options.text: Lift it myself — with good form
options.feedback: A compact 40 lb case is manageable solo for most people — form is everything.
Never wrong to use equipment! Slightly slower for one compact box, but zero strain.

options.text: Just bend over and yank it up fast
options.feedback: Bending at the waist and jerking a load is a classic back injury. Plan the lift and use your legs.

lifts.name: Long flat-pack box
lifts.prompt: A 6-foot flat-pack box. Not very heavy, but long and hard to balance.

options.text: Team lift — get a coworker on the other end
options.feedback: Awkward loads are as risky as heavy ones. A second person keeps it balanced and close.

options.text: Grab it in the middle and wing it
options.feedback: Long loads swing and twist your spine. Get help for awkward loads — then lift together.

lifts.name: Machine part crate
lifts.prompt: A 95 lb crate marked HEAVY. It needs to go across the floor to the pallet.

options.feedback: Exactly. Let equipment carry heavy loads — your back isn't a forklift.
Better than solo, but a hand truck is safer for both of you when one is available.

options.text: Lift it solo — I've got this
options.feedback: Heavy loads beyond what you can safely handle alone call for equipment or help. No heroics.

lifts.name: Box on the top shelf
lifts.prompt: A 25 lb box sits on a shelf above your head.

options.text: Use a step stool so the box is at chest height
options.feedback: Bringing yourself up to the load avoids lifting overhead, where you have the least control.

options.text: Reach up and pull it down over my head
options.feedback: Lifting overhead strains shoulders and back — and boxes fall on faces. Use a stool or platform.
Shelving isn't a ladder. Falls are one of the most common workplace injuries. Use a proper step stool.

lessons.far: Get close to the load before lifting — reaching out multiplies the strain on your back.
lessons.stoop: Bend at the knees, not the waist. Keep your back straight as you go down.
lessons.brace: Get a firm grip and tighten your core before the load leaves the ground.
lessons.jerk: Lift smoothly with your legs. Jerky, fast lifts are how backs get hurt.
lessons.twist: Step your feet round to face where the load is going — reaching and twisting under a load is how discs go.
lessons.drop: Lower the load the same way you lifted it: bend your knees and set it down under control.
lessons.yank: Plan every lift. Even a "quick" lift done bent over can injure your back.
lessons.awkward: Awkward or long loads need a team lift, even if they aren't very heavy.
lessons.heavy: Use a hand truck or get help for heavy loads — no heroics.
lessons.overhead: Avoid lifting above shoulder height. Use a step stool or platform.
lessons.climb: Never climb shelving — use a proper step stool or ladder.
lessons.perfect: Textbook lifting! Close, knees bent, back straight, smooth, pivot — every single time.
